object: cote 137 ('Dévissage des complexes 1/2 simpliciaux d-parfaits et structures multiplicatives', 1975 or 1976): titles, headings, page counts, reused sheets
statement: Local titles and headings; a cancelled upside-down sheet kept in the record; a reused Hirsch-method sheet and a Jacobian on reused paper with a limited evidential role; no authorial total page count.

object: d-perfect half-simplicial complexes: projectivity and flasqueness, perfection and specialness, pseudo-coherence, ranks and polynomial growth, torsion and Smith reduction, the classification up to isomorphism (cote 137 scans 2-44)
statement: A degreewise projective flasque simplicial module is projective (lemma, scan 2); specialness is stronger than perfection; ranks alone do not classify; the classification is up to isomorphism with invariant-factor normalization (per notes).

object: the devissage theorem: the walking complex and its universal property, Hom calculations, exact structures and the Ext group, density presentations, full faithfulness of evaluation, duality (cote 137 scans 2-86)
statement: Proposition 1 asserts an equivalence of categories; the opening theorem is revised and then argued; set-valued full faithfulness fails for finite sums (note R047) while the additive-envelope statement survives (R048); the duality is restricted to finite free components.

object: multiplicative structures on the coefficient models: transported tensor products, symmetric lax monoidal data, the unit (missing, then repaired by enlarging the category), cup products up to homotopy, divided-power and binomial operations, cosimplicial against DGA commutativity
statement: The missing unit is acknowledged and repaired; the cup product has its laws up to homotopy; the extension of stability to Lambda^i, Gamma^i, Sym^i is marked 'faux' in the margin (scan 10).

object: the de Rham comparison and integral reconstruction: weightwise and truncated comparisons, forward and reverse comparisons, integral homotopy reconstruction asked; binomial comparison (Toen, Horel); Burnside rings and Witt vectors
statement: Integral homotopy reconstruction is explicitly a question (scan 39); these pages do not establish it. Horel proves a precise binomial reconstruction theorem and Toen's integral points carry extra homotopy (literature, per notes).

object: polynomial laws and homogeneous functors: one-sided additivity, scalar actions, multilinear and strict representability, the tensor unit, multihomogeneous summands, exponential functors and Hopf structure, PD operations in degree zero, enrichment on Hom
statement: The author retracts scalar recognition of the grading; the announced equivalence is broader than the verified homogeneous core; degree zero is an acknowledged omission.

object: the author's own marks on cote 137: proposed axioms, withdrawn proof routes, unexpanded verifications, unit and enrichment questions

cote 138 ('Cartes. Etude arithmetique', catalogue date 1976, 77 ?): dating and documents: the 1980 subscription form, the June 1978 documents (a thesis notice, an administrative letter), the journal heading, authorial pagination, the descent title, the tower list
statement: The folder holds an order form 'Abonnement a Topologie structurale pour 1980 (N°s 4-6)' (scan 3) and documents dated 15 June 1978 (scan 43, a thesis defence set for 5 July 1978) and 22 June 1978 (scan 45). Dates on reused paper do not date every mathematical leaf.
status_on_pages: on the pages (checked against the transcription)
cross_topic: the dating of the dessins work; Belyi 1979

object: what cote 138 shows on maps, covers and curves over Qbar before Belyi (1979): the Galois action on finite cartographic sets, possible nontriviality, faithfulness, the converse 'every Qbar-curve'
statement: The Galois action on maps is a stated conclusion (BC03); 'may be nontrivial' does not assert faithfulness (BC05); the converse 'every Qbar-curve' is absent from scans 90-133 (BC06); regular-dessin faithfulness is a later, stronger theorem (BC08).
cross_topic: Esquisse d'un programme; La Longue Marche (cote 140); Belyi 1979

object: descent of covers and fields of definition (cote 138 scans 1-45): semilinear automorphisms, universal-cover automorphisms and the normalizer, field-of-definition images, descent of a covering pair, models over a fixed field, the central extension, H^1 and H^2, punctures and cross-ratio fields
statement: The splitting assertion includes an effectivity qualification; H^2 and H^1 are stated without a cocycle construction; several descent paragraphs are restarted.

object: explicit covers and Kummer calculations (cote 138 scans 18-45): branch values, root fibres, the torus image, the cyclotomic coefficient action, Kummer torsors, the affine Fermat cubic and its Tate module, the orientation torsor
statement: Torus image dimension and finite index remain author questions; a level-eight answer to the surjectivity question (note C07).

object: the cartographic tower (cote 138 scans 18-45): the genus list, the octahedral graph ('Sauf erreur'), the degree-two quotients, barycentric subdivision, the tower title sheet; arithmetic images: finite witnesses, scalar Tate actions, congruence kernels
status_on_pages: programme on the title sheet; parts computed

object: the tower of cote 138 scans 46-89: groupoids of punctured spheres ('a bouts', later 'a lacets'), operator groups T_nu, orientation modules, fibre-functor torsors, Galois transport and the cyclotomic character, cross-rank isomorphisms
statement: The cross-rank isomorphisms are a wish, not a conclusion; surjectivity is asserted twice without proof; rank one is an exception to the inner injection (notes).
cross_topic: La Longue Marche (cote 140-2): 22 notes of this packet relate these scans to LM140-2

object: explicit covers in cote 138 scans 46-89: the three-point cover, mu_infinity, the cubic identity on the conic, the odd power, critical values, the bipyramid, tame signatures, the cancelled wild excursion, the genus-zero check of the Kummer reduction, seven marked points, Fermat examples
statement: The genus-zero check in the Kummer reduction is explicitly unfinished; the Fermat examples do not decide the CM character problem.

object: the profinite sphere and braid groups with Galois action (cote 138 scans 90-133): the oriented quotient, completion against closure, normality of the completed discrete subgroup, the weighted peripheral presentation, commutants and twisting of the torsor system, cyclotomic inertia, the comparison torsor
statement: The author withdraws the equality at nu = 2; identifying the quotient with Aut(I_i) needs surjectivity.

object: moduli of maps and the low-degree catalogue: pinnings, the rigidity claim, counting with orbit sizes, the raw moduli functor, relabelling stabilizers, group-type strata, the catalogue's group labels, passports, chirality, the 'impossible' annotations
statement: The unrestricted rigidity claim is false (MM02) while genus-zero geometric rigidity survives (MM04); the degree-five 'rigide' map is chiral; a repeated passport can encode distinct maps; a degree-six heading is numerically inconsistent as frozen (MM17).
status_on_pages: catalogue on the pages; claims corrected by the notes

object: explicit small Belyi maps (cote 138 scans 100-113): the seven small maps and their ramification, the barycentric equation, co-pinnings of the cubic star and the mod-3 cyclotomic character, permutation tables generating S_6, the admissible cubic with S_3 and Q(2^{1/3})
statement: Two co-pinnings of the cubic star detect the mod-3 cyclotomic character; the numerator sign on scan 109 and the factor two of the quadratic roots are reading questions.
status_on_pages: computed on the pages; checked in part by the notes

object: operations on maps (cote 138 scans 113-133): the provisional axioms, rigidification of maps on the sphere, isotopy kernels, the face-order classification, 'oranges', holomorphic models, arithmetic equivariance, the sextic family
statement: The claimed rigidity of oranges is false (OP33) and the tentative exception list incomplete (OP35); the face-order classification omits a two-loop map (OP32); the sextic family gives a non-equivariant operation (OP44).
status_on_pages: programme; claims corrected by the notes
